# bgraph reference

<!-- Generated by `bgraph docs`. Edit src/docgen.rs, not this file. -->

Diagrams as text, where **you** decide the layout.

Mermaid and friends auto-place everything and leave you fighting the engine.
`bgraph` inverts that: every node says where it goes, but says it *relative to
its neighbours* — so you keep control without hand-editing coordinates every
time the diagram grows.

- A prose introduction lives in [`../README.md`](../README.md).
- A worked tour of the syntax lives in [`language.md`](language.md).
- **This file is the exhaustive reference**, generated from the compiler's own
  tables, so it always describes the binary you have.

## Commands

```
bgraph diagram.bd -o diagram.svg    # render
bgraph watch diagram.bd             # live preview on :7878, reloads on save
bgraph watch diagram.bd --port 9000
bgraph check diagram.bd             # diagnostics only; non-zero on error
bgraph docs -o docs/reference.md    # regenerate this file
bgraph-lsp                          # language server, LSP over stdin/stdout
```

## The five statements

```
type <archetype> { … }      // the genre of diagram; optional, defaults to free
graph { … }                 // diagram-wide settings
style <name> [extends <name>] { … }
group <id> ["<label>"] [.class …] [<placement>] { … }
<keyword> <id> ["<label>"] <data…> [.class …] [<placement>] { … }
<id> <arrow> <id> ["<label>"] [.class …] { … }
```

The fourth is an **item**, and each archetype has its own word for it —
`node` in `free`, `slice` in `pie`, `field` in `packet`. `node` stays a
universal synonym everywhere, so nothing is ever forced.

```
type pie
slice organic "Organic search" 4820
slice referral 1180                    // no label: the id is displayed
node b "Direct" { value: 2410 }        // the long form, still valid
```

Values after the label fill the archetype's slots in order, and are **sugar
for the properties it declares** — `slice a 4820` and `slice a { value: 4820 }`
build the same thing. The first string after the identifier is always the
label, so an archetype whose data is a string obliges you to write one.

A statement runs to its separator. `node a node b` on one line is therefore
one item with two stray values, not two items, and `check` says so.

Statements are separated by newlines; `;` and `,` also work. Comments start
with `//` — `#` is reserved for hex colors and cannot also open a comment.

Identifiers may contain letters, digits, `_` and an interior `-`. A trailing
hyphen is not allowed, which is what lets `a->b` split into three tokens.
The four statement keywords — `type`, `graph`, `style`, `node` — are reserved
and cannot name a node.

Labels are quoted. `\n` splits a label into centred lines; `\t` and `\"` also
work. A node with no label falls back to its identifier. Label text is
XML-escaped on output, so `<`, `&` and quotes are safe.

## Groups

A `group` is a frame. Its block holds properties *and* nested statements, so
groups nest:

```
group edge "Edge" {
  padding: 22
  node gw   "Gateway"
  node auth "Auth" below gw gap 30
}

group core "Core" right-of edge gap 60 {
  node orders "Orders"
}

node db "Postgres" right-of core gap 60
```

**A group is sized by its members, never the other way round** — its rectangle
is their bounding box plus its `padding`. That keeps the rule this language is
built on: the items say where they go.

A group may still carry a placement, and then it **translates its whole
subtree** once its members have landed. Members of a placed group only become
anchorable after that translation, so nothing outside can latch onto a
position that is about to move.

Groups and items share one namespace, so a group can be anchored to by name.
An edge to a group is refused — a frame has no obvious endpoint. Style them
with `style group { … }` or a `.class`; the default is a dashed border, a
transparent fill and the label set into the top-left.

## Placement

| Form | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `at (x, y)` | absolute top-left corner |
| `right-of <id>` | to the right of another node |
| `left-of <id>` | to its left |
| `below <id>` | underneath it |
| `above <id>` | over it |
| `gap <n>` | distance to the anchor; defaults to the graph `gap` |
| `align <kw>` | cross-axis alignment against the anchor |

Anchors may point **forward**: the solver runs repeated passes, so a node may
be anchored to one declared later. A genuine loop is reported as an error.

A node with no placement flows from the previous one in source order, using
the graph's `flow` direction and `gap`. The first node lands at `(0, 0)`.

Sizes come from the label plus `padding` unless `size`, `width` or `height`
says otherwise. The canvas is derived from the content — nothing is ever
clipped, and negative coordinates are fine.

## Arrows

| Token | Line | Heads |
|---|---|---|
| `->` | solid | end |
| `<-` | solid | start |
| `<->` | solid | both |
| `--` | solid | none |
| `-->` | dashed | end |
| `..>` | dotted | end |
| `..` | dotted | none |

The token's dash pattern is a default; `{ dash: solid }` overrides it.

## Colors

`#rgb`, `#rgba`, `#rrggbb`, `#rrggbbaa`, or an SVG color name (`white`,
`tomato`).

**The fourth channel is the alpha**, and it defaults to `ff` — opaque. There
is no separate `opacity` property: transparency belongs to the color that
carries it, which is what lets a shape have an opaque border and a translucent
fill.

```
node card "Card" {
  fill: #1e293b80      // half-transparent slate
  stroke: #38bdf8      // fully opaque, alpha omitted
  font-color: #e2e8f0c0
}
```

On output the alpha becomes its own attribute — `fill="#1e293b" fill-opacity="0.5"`
rather than an eight-digit hex. Both render identically in a modern viewer, but
several SVG-to-PDF paths and older renderers drop the inline alpha silently.

Note that this is per-paint, not per-element: a translucent fill lets the inner
half of a thick stroke show through, which a single element opacity would have
composited away first.

## The style cascade

```
built-in defaults  →  style node / style edge  →  .classes (in order)  →  inline { }
```

The implicit theme is the archetype's own word — `style slice { … }` in a
pie — with `style node` and `style edge` remaining universal aliases, applied
first so the specific name wins where both are declared. `extends` flattens a chain
child-first. An unknown property or an unknown `.class` is an error.

## Property reference

Every property below is valid on a `style` block, on a `node` or edge statement's inline block, or both. Anything else is an error, not a silent no-op — a typo surfaces the moment you save.

Aliases are marked. They behave identically to the property they alias; the editor keeps them out of completion so the list stays short.

| Property | Applies to | Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fill` | node | `fill: <color>` | Interior color of the shape. |
| `background` *(alias)* | node | `background: <color>` | Alias of `fill`. |
| `stroke` | both | `stroke: <color> <width> <solid\|dashed\|dotted>` | Outline. Accepts a color, a width and a dash pattern in any order; omit whichever you don't need. |
| `border` *(alias)* | both | `border: <color> <width> <pattern>` | Alias of `stroke`. |
| `color` *(alias)* | both | `color: <color> <width> <pattern>` | Alias of `stroke`. For text color use `font-color`. |
| `stroke-width` | both | `stroke-width: <number>` | Outline thickness in user units. |
| `weight` *(alias)* | both | `weight: <number>` | Alias of `stroke-width`. |
| `dash` | both | `dash: <solid\|dashed\|dotted> \| dash: <on> <off>` | Dash pattern. Named, or explicit on/off lengths such as `dash: 6 3`. |
| `radius` | node | `radius: <number>` | Corner rounding — applies to the `rect` shape. |
| `corner` *(alias)* | node | `corner: <number>` | Alias of `radius`. |
| `shape` | node | `shape: <rect\|stadium\|ellipse\|diamond\|hexagon\|cylinder>` | Outline geometry. Edge endpoints are clipped against it. |
| `size` | node | `size: <width> <height>` | Fixed size. Without it the box is sized from the label and `padding`. |
| `width` | node | `width: <number>` | Fixed width; the height still follows the label. |
| `height` | node | `height: <number>` | Fixed height; the width still follows the label. |
| `padding` | node | `padding: <number>` | Inset between the label and the outline; drives the auto-size. |
| `font` | both | `font: <size> "<family>" <color> <weight>` | Shorthand read by value kind, so the order is free: a number is the size, a string the family, a color the ink, a bare word the weight. |
| `font-size` | both | `font-size: <number>` | Text size in user units. |
| `font-family` | both | `font-family: "<family>"` | Font stack, emitted verbatim into the SVG. |
| `font-color` | both | `font-color: <color>` | Text color. |
| `text-color` *(alias)* | both | `text-color: <color>` | Alias of `font-color`. |
| `font-weight` | both | `font-weight: <weight>` | Any SVG weight — `400`, `bold`, `600`… |
| `arrow` | edge | `arrow: <solid\|open\|dot\|none>` | Arrow head style. The arrow token decides which ends carry one. |
| `head` *(alias)* | edge | `head: <solid\|open\|dot\|none>` | Alias of `arrow`. |
| `router` | edge | `router: <straight\|ortho>` | `straight` draws a direct line; `ortho` draws a right-angled elbow. |
| `route` *(alias)* | edge | `route: <straight\|ortho>` | Alias of `router`. |
| `value` | both | `value: <number>` | Magnitude of a slice. Required by `type pie`, ignored elsewhere. |
| `wave` | node | `wave: "<characters>"` | One character per period: `0` `1` `l` `h` levels, `p` `n` clocks, `x` unknown, `z` high-impedance, `=` and `2`–`9` data, `.` repeats the previous, `\|` a gap. Required by `type wave`. |
| `data` | node | `data: "<first>" "<second>" …` | Names for the data segments of a wave, in order. |
| `x` | node | `x: <number>` | Horizontal position. Required by `type quadrant`, ignored elsewhere. |
| `y` | node | `y: <number>` | Vertical position. Required by `type quadrant`, ignored elsewhere. |
| `bits` | node | `bits: <first> <last>` | Inclusive bit range of a field. Required by `type packet`, ignored elsewhere; `bits: 8` is shorthand for a single bit. |
| `shadow` | node | `shadow: <on\|off>` | Soft drop shadow under the shape. |

## Graph settings

Declared once, in `graph { … }`. These are diagram-wide and are not part of the style cascade.

| Setting | Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `padding` | `padding: <number>` | Margin between the drawing and the canvas edge. |
| `gap` | `gap: <number>` | Default distance used by anchors that omit `gap`. |
| `background` | `background: <color>` | Canvas fill. Also backs edge labels so they stay readable. |
| `bg` *(alias)* | `bg: <color>` | Alias of `background`. |
| `flow` | `flow: <right\|left\|down\|up>` | Direction used to place nodes that declare no placement. |
| `direction` *(alias)* | `direction: <right\|left\|down\|up>` | Alias of `flow`. |

The surface is **explicit by default**: without a `background` the renderer still paints `#ffffff`, so the live preview and the exported file agree. Write `background: none` (or `transparent`) for a transparent SVG — the preview then shows a checkerboard rather than pretending.

## Archetypes

`type` picks the genre of diagram, once, at the top of the file. Without it the file is `free`.

Every archetype reads the *same* statements: a `node` is a box, a slice or a bitfield depending on the genre. The style cascade, the diagnostics and the editor support are identical in all of them — what changes is which properties carry meaning.

### `type free`

Nodes and edges placed by anchors — the default when a file declares no `type`.

```
node <id> ["label"]
```

It takes no settings.

### `type pie`

A pie or donut chart. Each slice needs a value; its `fill` overrides the automatic palette.

```
slice <id> ["label"] <value>
```

| Setting | Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `title: <text>` | Heading drawn above the chart. |
| `radius` | `radius: <number>` | Outer radius in user units. |
| `donut` | `donut: <0..1>` | Inner hole as a fraction of the radius. `0` is a full pie. |
| `start` | `start: <degrees>` | Angle the first slice starts at. `0` is twelve o'clock. |
| `labels` | `labels: <percent\|value\|both\|none>` | What to write on each slice. Slices too thin to read are skipped. |
| `legend` | `legend: <on\|off>` | Swatch-and-name list beside the chart. On by default — identity must never rest on color alone. |

### `type sankey`

Flows between stages, sized by magnitude. The value rides on the link, not on what it joins: a node's height is whatever passes through it.

```
node <id> ["label"]
```

| Setting | Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `title: <text>` | Heading drawn above the diagram. |
| `size` | `size: <width> <height>` | The area the flows fill. 680 by 400 by default. |
| `gap` | `gap: <number>` | Space between stacked nodes in a column. |
| `width` | `width: <number>` | Thickness of a node bar. |
| `labels` | `labels: <name\|value\|both\|none>` | What to write beside each node. |

### `type wave`

A timing diagram. Each signal carries a wave string, one character per period, in the WaveDrom alphabet.

```
signal <id> ["label"] <wave>
```

| Setting | Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `title: <text>` | Heading drawn above the lanes. |
| `period` | `period: <number>` | Width of one wave character. 40 by default. |
| `lane` | `lane: <height> <gap>` | Height of a signal lane and the space beneath it. |
| `ruler` | `ruler: <on\|off>` | Period numbers above the lanes. On by default. |
| `every` | `every: <number>` | Label a ruler tick every N periods. 4 by default. |
| `grid` | `grid: <on\|off>` | Vertical lines on the period boundaries. On by default. |

### `type quadrant`

Points on two axes, divided into four named regions. A Wardley map is this archetype with its own axis names.

```
point <id> ["label"] <x> <y>
```

| Setting | Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `title: <text>` | Heading drawn above the chart. |
| `size` | `size: <width> <height>` | The plot area. 460 square by default. |
| `range` | `range: <min> <max>` | The span both axes cover. `0 1` by default. |
| `x-axis` | `x-axis: "<left>" "<right>"` | What the horizontal axis means at each end. |
| `y-axis` | `y-axis: "<bottom>" "<top>"` | What the vertical axis means at each end. |
| `quadrants` | `quadrants: "<top-right>" "<top-left>" "<bottom-left>" "<bottom-right>"` | Names for the four regions, anticlockwise from the top right. |
| `labels` | `labels: <name\|none>` | Whether each point carries its name. |

### `type treemap`

Nested rectangles whose area is proportional to a value. The hierarchy is group nesting; a group's area is the sum of what it contains.

```
box <id> ["label"] <value>
```

| Setting | Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `title: <text>` | Heading drawn above the map. |
| `size` | `size: <width> <height>` | The rectangle the map fills. 640 by 400 by default. |
| `gap` | `gap: <number>` | Surface showing between sibling tiles. Adjacent fills must never touch, so this is 2 by default and never 0. |
| `header` | `header: <number>` | Height reserved inside a group's tile for its name. |
| `labels` | `labels: <name\|value\|both\|none>` | What to write on each tile. Tiles too small to read are skipped. |

### `type packet`

A packet / bitfield diagram. Each field needs an inclusive bit range; one crossing a row boundary is split across rows.

```
field <id> ["label"] <bits> <bits>
```

| Setting | Syntax | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `title` | `title: <text>` | Heading drawn above the diagram. |
| `width` | `width: <bits>` | Bits per row. 32 by default. |
| `cell` | `cell: <width> <height>` | Width of one bit and the height of a row. |
| `ruler` | `ruler: <on\|off>` | Bit indices above each row. On by default. |

Edges and placement are ignored by the chart archetypes — and reported, not
silently dropped.

`style node { … }` is the only text hook a chart has, so it governs the
title, the on-slice labels and the legend alike. On-slice text defaults to
white, which reads on all eight palette hues; everything else defaults to the
theme's ink for the surface.

## Accepted words

**Shapes** — `rect` · `box` · `rectangle` · `stadium` · `pill` · `rounded` · `ellipse` · `circle` · `oval` · `diamond` · `rhombus` · `decision` · `hexagon` · `hex` · `cylinder` · `database` · `db`

Several names denote the same shape; pick whichever reads best.

**Arrow heads** — `solid` · `filled` · `triangle` · `open` · `line` · `thin` · `dot` · `circle` · `none`

Used by `arrow:` on an edge.

**Routers** — `straight` · `direct` · `line` · `ortho` · `orthogonal` · `elbow`

Used by `router:` on an edge.

**Dash patterns** — `solid` · `dashed` · `dotted` · `none`

Accepted by `dash:` and inside a compound `stroke:`.

**Alignments** — `left` · `right` · `center` · `middle` · `top` · `bottom`

Used by `align` in a placement. `left`/`right` for a vertical placement, `top`/`bottom` for a horizontal one, `center` (or `middle`) for either — and the default.

**Flow directions** — `right` · `left` · `down` · `up` · `LR` · `RL` · `TB` · `BT`

Used by `flow:` in `graph { … }`, for nodes that declare no placement.

**Pie labels** — `percent` · `value` · `both` · `none`

Used by `labels:` in `type pie { … }`.

### Categorical palette

Pie slices that declare no `fill` take these hues, in order, never cycled. Two columns of the same eight hues, stepped for a light or a dark `background`; the renderer picks the column from the surface's luminance.

The order is validated: worst adjacent-pair separation is ΔE 9.1 for protanopia on light and 8.4 on dark (OKLab ×100, ≥ 8 target), and 19.6 / 19.3 for normal vision (≥ 15 floor).

| Slot | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `#2a78d6` | `#3987e5` |
| 2 | `#eb6834` | `#d95926` |
| 3 | `#1baf7a` | `#199e70` |
| 4 | `#eda100` | `#c98500` |
| 5 | `#e87ba4` | `#d55181` |
| 6 | `#008300` | `#008300` |
| 7 | `#4a3aa7` | `#9085e9` |
| 8 | `#e34948` | `#e66767` |

There is no ninth hue. Past eight slices `check` tells you to merge the tail into an `Other` slice rather than repeat a color.

## Diagnostics

`check` and the language server report exactly the same things — one
validator serves both, so the editor can never disagree with the build.

**Errors**

- an unknown property, style, node, shape, router, arrow head or archetype
  (property typos come with a suggestion)
- a node declared twice, or `type` declared twice
- a node named after a statement keyword (`type`, `graph`, `style`, `node`) —
  an edge cannot start with one, so the name would be half-usable at best
- a node anchored to itself, or a cycle of anchors
- a style that extends an unknown style, or extends itself in a cycle
- a property with no value
- `type pie` — a node with no `value`, or a negative one
- `type packet` — a node with no `bits`, or ranges that overlap

**Warnings**

- a property with no effect where it is written (`shape` on an edge,
  `value` outside `type pie`, a setting on an archetype that takes none)
- a style declared more than once
- text whose contrast against what sits behind it is below 3:1
- `type pie` — a slice with value 0; fewer than three slices, which a bar or
  a single number compares better; more than eight, which exhausts the palette
- `type packet` — bits left unassigned between two fields
- an edge or a placement in an archetype that ignores it

## Editor support

`bgraph-lsp` speaks LSP over stdin/stdout with no arguments, so any client can
use it. A Zed extension is packaged in [`../editors/zed`](../editors/zed)
together with a tree-sitter grammar.

It provides diagnostics, go-to-definition from any reference to its
declaration, a symbol outline, hover (a property's syntax and meaning, a
node's label and **resolved position and size**, a style's flattened property
list), and context-aware completion.

Completion is deliberately quiet: it never fires inside a label or a comment,
`.` only opens the style list where a class reference can actually go, aliases
are hidden, and `value` / `bits` appear only under the archetype that reads
them.

## Grammar

The authoritative grammar is [`../src/syntax.pest`](../src/syntax.pest); the
tree-sitter grammar in [`../tree-sitter-bgraph`](../tree-sitter-bgraph) mirrors
it and is covered by a corpus test suite.

Two details are worth knowing because they shape the syntax:

- Newlines separate statements, so horizontal whitespace and newlines are not
  interchangeable.
- Inside a `{ }` block, a property's value list ends at the next `name:`. That
  is what lets `{ fill: #111 stroke: #222 }` sit on one line.
